title_candidates: Turn a LaTeX equation into a shareable link in five minutes
Simon Willison's LaTeX renderer makes equations easy to share
summary: A free browser tool turns LaTeX equations and documents into live previews, shareable links, images, or PDFs. A five-minute test shows what the link contains before you send it.

primary_source.title: Tool: LaTeX renderer
primary_source.author: Simon Willison
key_facts: LaTeX renderer turns a bare formula into a MathJax display equation and can also render prose fragments or full documents with faster-latex.
The browser interface pairs source editing with a live preview and lets readers switch between Edit and Rendered views.
Readers can type LaTeX, load it from a public URL or GitHub Gist, or start from built-in equation and document examples.
The tool places the LaTeX in the URL fragment, creating readable or compressed links that can reopen the same material without an account.
Willison says Claude Code using Opus 5.5 Extra built the tool in his existing public tools repository.
Willison asked for the rendered result to run in a sandboxed iframe, reusing a protection pattern from his SVG-in-Markdown tool.
The implementation uses MathJax, faster-latex, Pako, and DOMPurify in the browser.

supporting_sources.title: LaTeX renderer
key_facts: The live tool offers built-in examples, live editing, Edit and Rendered views, URL or GitHub Gist loading, and readable or compressed share links.
Its export controls can copy the LaTeX, copy the rendered image, download PNG or SVG, or open the browser's print-to-PDF path.
The tool states that its readable and compressed links contain the LaTeX itself.

supporting_sources.title: Tools colophon: LaTeX renderer
key_facts: The public development record identifies the tool as AI generated and links the single implementation commit and Claude Code transcript.
The colophon confirms MathJax for equations, faster-latex for prose and documents, and PNG, SVG, and print-to-PDF export paths.
It records the deliberate reuse of sandbox and URL-loading patterns from the older Markdown SVG tool.

supporting_sources.title: latex.html source code
key_facts: The public source configures rendered documents in a sandboxed iframe and applies a restrictive content-security policy.
External URL loading is initiated by the reader and uses credential-free, no-referrer fetching; the page still loads its rendering libraries from third-party CDNs.

prerequisites: A modern browser with JavaScript enabled
No account or LaTeX installation required

steps.instruction: Open the LaTeX renderer, select the Quadratic formula example, and confirm the editor fills while the preview shows a typeset equation with an Equation / MathJax label.
Replace the first x in the source with y, confirm the live preview updates, then select Rendered to show the clean equation view.

Select Copy link, paste the copied URL into a new browser tab, and confirm the same equation opens without an account or saved document. The link contains the LaTeX, so do not use confidential material.
Select Share, download PNG or SVG, and open the downloaded file to confirm the equation exported as an image. Use Print / save PDF only if you need a document-style copy.

risk_flags: Readable and compressed share links contain the LaTeX itself; anyone with the link can read it, so the guide excludes confidential material.
The page runs rendering in a sandboxed iframe but still loads libraries from third-party CDNs, so it is not described as fully offline.

The interaction pattern overlaps Signal's August Markdown SVG Renderer guide; this article stays narrowly focused on equations, LaTeX-specific examples, self-contained formula links, and math image export.
